what_its_for: Ribavirin is an antiviral medicine used to treat chronic hepatitis C infection. It is almost always used together with other antiviral medicines — it is rarely used alone. Your doctor will tell you exactly which medicines you are taking as part of your treatment plan.
how_to_take: Take ribavirin by mouth with food to help reduce stomach upset and improve how well your body absorbs the medicine. Swallow capsules or tablets whole — do not crush, break, or chew them. Take your doses at the same times each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Always take ribavirin exactly as your doctor prescribed. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
dosing: Your dose depends on your body weight, the form of ribavirin you are taking, and the other medicines in your treatment plan. A common adult dose ranges from 800 mg to 1,200 mg per day, usually split into a morning dose and an evening dose. Your doctor will set the exact dose that is right for you. Never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within a few hours of when you were supposed to take it. If it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store ribavirin capsules or tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you have leftover medicine after finishing your treatment, ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Do not take ribavirin if you are pregnant or if your partner is pregnant — ribavirin causes serious birth defects and can harm an unborn baby. Both men and women must use two reliable forms of birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking ribavirin. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can make liver problems worse. Do not take antacids containing magnesium or aluminum within 2 hours of your dose, as they may reduce how well ribavirin works. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or tired. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you are taking ribavirin before any procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe tiredness, chest pain, shortness of breath, or irregular heartbeat (signs of anemia or heart problems); signs of depression such as feeling very sad, hopeless, or having thoughts of hurting yourself; fever, chills, or signs of infection; sudden or severe stomach pain; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bruising or bleeding; vision changes or eye pain; severe skin rash or itching; or if you or your partner becomes pregnant during treatment. Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room if you have a life-threatening emergency.
when_it_works: Ribavirin starts working right away to fight the hepatitis C virus, but you will not feel or see this happening. It often takes several weeks of treatment before lab tests show the virus levels dropping. Most people complete a course of treatment lasting 12 to 48 weeks depending on their specific situation. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to check how well the treatment is working and to monitor your safety throughout the process.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Ribavirin must NOT be used during pregnancy. It causes serious birth defects. Pregnancy must be ruled out before starting, and reliable birth control must be used during treatment and for 6 months after. Men: If your female partner could become pregnant, you must also use two forms of birth control during and for 6 months after treatment. Kidney problems: Ribavirin may not be safe if you have moderate to severe kidney disease. Your doctor will decide if it is right for you. Older adults (65+): Use with extra caution, as older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as anemia. Children: Ribavirin is approved for children aged 3 years and older in certain situations; the dose is based on the child's weight. Heart disease: Use with caution if you have a history of heart problems, as ribavirin can worsen anemia and put extra strain on the heart.
